findings.claim: "In the Edexcel 1ET0 Component 1, Section B exam... The essay is worth 25 marks and assesses AO1... AO3... AO4" (repeated in L8 conclusion_html: "Section B is a 25-mark essay").
findings.truth: The post-1914 British play essay is worth 40 marks: AO1 16, AO3 16, AO4 8. The 25-mark figure is not an Edexcel mark total for any question on this qualification. The same sentence also carries two strings the house validator rejects, the spec code and the component label.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md, assessment summary (Component 1 Section B, ONE essay from a choice of two, marks for SPaG, AO1/AO3/AO4) and the raw-mark distribution table: questions 7-30 = AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8 = 40.

findings.claim: "How many marks is the Section B Blood Brothers essay worth?" options 15/20/25/30, answer key marks "25 marks" correct.
findings.truth: 40 marks. The right answer was not even among the options, so every student was marked on a false key. Options rewritten to 20/25/30/40 with 40 correct.
On this question AO1 and AO3 are equal at 16 marks each, with 8 for AO4. Telling students AO1 outweighs context encourages them to under-write the AO3 material this question is built around.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md, Breakdown of Assessment Objectives by component.

findings.claim: Mrs Lyons: "If either twin was told he was one of a pair, they shall both immediately die." Used nine times across L2 and L8 (content, key fact, quotation list, quotation bank, two practice stimuli, two flashcards).
findings.truth: The line is "They say...they say that if either twin learns that he once was a pair, that they shall both immediately die." The curse turns on the twins LEARNING the truth. Corrected to "if either twin learns that he once was a pair... they shall both immediately die".
findings.evidence: LitCharts Blood Brothers quotes, Mrs Lyons, Act 1 p.47 (https://www.litcharts.com/lit/blood-brothers/quotes); GradeSaver quotes page gives the same line as "if either twin learns that he was once a pair" - the two sources differ only on once was / was once, so the shortened form avoids that clause.

findings.claim: "The Narrator reveals that twin brothers 'were born, and died, on the self same day.'" and "Did you ever hear the story of the Johnstone twins?" (the first also on flashcard 1).
findings.truth: The opening runs "So did y'hear the story of the Johnstone twins? / As like each other as two new pins, / Of one womb born, on the self same day...". "Born, and died, on the self same day" is a fabricated composite, and it also states a plot untruth: the twins are born on one day and die as adults, roughly twenty-five years later.
findings.evidence: LitCharts Blood Brothers quotes, Narrator, Act 1 p.29; GradeSaver quotes page, Overture.

findings.claim: "Eddie exclaims that they are 'almost like real brothers'" - in a Key Fact, its revision tip, and a flashcard that asks which phrase Eddie uses.
findings.truth: No such line exists. The birthday moment is Mickey's: "Ey, we were born on the same day...that means we can be blood brothers." Both the wording and the speaker were wrong, so the flashcard drilled an invented quotation.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver Blood Brothers quotes, attributed to Mickey; LitCharts quotes page confirms the phrase "almost like real brothers" appears nowhere.

findings.claim: "Mickey's reaction to Eddie's posh vocabulary ('You say smashing things, don't you?')".
findings.truth: Eddie says this to Mickey, delighted by Mickey's slang and swearing. The lesson contradicts itself: an earlier paragraph and knowledge check 2 both put the line in Eddie's mouth.
findings.evidence: L3 content_html n11 and knowledge_checks[1] in the same lesson; LitCharts Act 1 summary (Edward is fascinated by Mickey's language).

findings.claim: "Sammy shoots a cat with an air rifle" - stated in L3, L6 and L7 content, in an L3 knowledge-check match item, and in three practice mark schemes and a flashcard.
findings.truth: Sammy shoots no cat and has no air rifle. His childhood violence is stealing Mickey's toy gun, bullying, urinating on sweets, and burning the school down. L6 also invents "he burns a teacher's desk" for the school fire.
findings.evidence: LitCharts Act 1 summary and Sammy Johnstone character page (https://www.litcharts.com/lit/blood-brothers/characters/sammy-johnstone): stolen toy gun, burned the school down, no cat and no air rifle. GradeSaver plot summary likewise.

findings.claim: "Linda urges him: 'Take a pill, Mickey. They'll wash your cares away.'" - plus a paragraph analysing the phrase, three practice-question stimuli (L4, L5, L8), a knowledge-check fill item, a flashcard, and the L8 quotation bank.
findings.truth: The line does not exist and it reverses Linda's role. Linda begs Mickey to STOP taking the antidepressants; he refuses, saying he cannot cope without them. A student who used this in an essay would be describing the opposite of the scene.
findings.evidence: LitCharts Act 2 summary: "Linda begs Mickey to stop taking pills, but he refuses... he can't function without the pills"; LitCharts symbols page (Mickey's antidepressants).

findings.claim: The glossary term "Mrs Lyons" is defined as "A character whose qualities contrast with another character, highlighting their differences."
findings.truth: That is the definition of a foil, not of Mrs Lyons. L6 uses the same definition correctly under the term "foil". The dfn now wraps "foil" and the glossary entry is renamed.
findings.evidence: Internal: L6 glossary_terms and content_html n6 use the identical definition for "foil".

findings.claim: The glossary term "dramatic device" is defined as "A narrative technique that hints at future events, creating a sense of anticipation or dread."
findings.truth: That defines foreshadowing. A dramatic device is any technique a playwright uses to shape the audience's response. The definition is corrected in the dfn and the glossary.
findings.evidence: Internal glossary conflict: the same definition is given for "foreshadowing" in L2 glossary_terms.

findings.claim: "A Level 5 response will discuss..." (L7); "discuss it explicitly to hit AO1." (L3 exam tip); flashcard answers "AO1.", "AO3.", "AO4." (L8).
findings.truth: All five strings match the house validator's banned patterns (Level N band names, and an AO code followed by a full stop). They would reject the whole unit on the next write, and "Level 5" is not a band name any student should learn.

findings.claim: "struggling to feed seven (then eight, then nine) children".
findings.truth: She has seven children and is expecting twins. Nine are born, Edward is given away, so she raises eight. The bracketed run counts upward to a total she never has.
findings.evidence: LitCharts Act 1 summary: "By the time she was twenty-five, Mrs. Johnstone had seven children and was pregnant again"; L6 flashcard 3 in this lesson says seven.

findings.claim: Every one of the 48 practice questions is labelled "40 marks - Post-1914 Essay" but carries a mark ladder that runs to 25: "Top band (21-25) ... Top band (16-20) ... Upper-mid band (11-15) ... Lower-mid band (6-10) ... Lower band (1-5)". The top label is also duplicated.
findings.truth: The question is 40 marks and the ladder must reach 40. Rewritten across all 8 lessons to the house ladder in five equal bands: Top band (33-40), Upper-mid band (25-32), Mid band (17-24), Lower-mid band (9-16), Low band (1-8). Descriptor text is unchanged.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md raw-mark distribution table; the questions' own type label.

findings.claim: The stimulus "'bright new day... we went dancing.'" (L2 question 6, L4 question 3) is printed as one quotation.
findings.truth: These are two lines from two different songs: "Oh a bright new day, we're moving away" (Bright New Day, Act 2) and "we went dancing" (Marilyn Monroe, Act 1). The ellipsis makes them read as one continuous line. Either split them and name both songs, or replace the stimulus with a single real line. Not edited because the choice of replacement changes what the question asks. ORCHESTRATOR: replaced both stimuli with the single verified line "Oh a bright new day, we're moving away."
findings.evidence: GradeSaver quotes page lists "Oh a bright new day, / We're moving away" under Bright New Day - Reprise and the dancing refrain under Marilyn Monroe.

findings.claim: Stimulus quotations "'We're blood brothers now.'" (L3, L6, L8), "'That's what bein' a blood brother means.'" (L3), and "'Give one to me, Mrs Johnstone.'" (L1, L2, L6, L8).
findings.truth: None of the sources reached carry these exact strings. They are plausible renderings of real moments - Mickey's words at the pin ritual, and Mrs Lyons' request for a twin - and the vocative "Mrs Johnstone" may be an addition to "Give one to me." Left alone: the rule is to correct a quotation only once the real wording is found, and no source consulted printed these lines either way.
findings.evidence: LitCharts quotes page and GradeSaver quotes page carry neither string; both do confirm the surrounding scenes.

findings.claim: Match item: "North-South divide" pairs with "Eddie's southern university education contrasts with Mickey's northern poverty".
findings.truth: The play never says where Edward studies. The match still works, but a student could repeat "southern university" as fact in an essay. Not worth an edit, because removing the word breaks the pairing logic the item is built on.
findings.evidence: No source consulted places Edward's university; LitCharts and GradeSaver both say only that he goes to university.

findings.claim: "Allow yourself roughly 45 minutes for this essay... 5 minutes planning and 40 minutes writing" (and the matching flashcard).
findings.truth: The paper runs 1 hour 45 minutes for 80 marks in two sections worth 40 marks each, so an even split is closer to 50 minutes. The text does tell students to check the specimen paper, and timing advice is not a spec claim, so it is left as written.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md assessment summary: 1 hour 45 minutes, 80 marks, Section A two-part question and Section B essay.

summary: Every lesson carried at least one real error. The unit taught the wrong mark total for its own exam question (25 instead of 40, including a knowledge check whose right answer was not on the list), and four fabricated or misattributed quotations were drilled through content, quotation banks, stimuli, knowledge checks and flashcards - the worst being an invented Linda line that reverses her role over Mickey's antidepressants. 96 edits written across all 8 lessons, 48 of them the mark-ladder rewrite.
